Seagate price target raised as Bank of America sees strong demand for hard drives Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Seagate Technology Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:STX) is positioned for stronger revenue and earnings growth as demand for hard disk drives (HDDs) outpaces the company's long-term expectations, according to Bank of America, which raised its price target on the stock to $1,200 from $1,150.

The bank reiterated its Buy rating, forecasting first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue at the high end of management's guidance and earnings above its projected range.

Bank of America expects revenue of $4.2 billion for the September quarter, against company guidance of $4 billion to $4.2 billion, and earnings per share of $7.60, above the guided range of $7.10 to $7.50. Wall Street consensus stands at $4.14 billion in revenue and $7.41 in earnings per share.

The analysts expect continued pricing strength, forecasting revenue per terabyte to rise about 22% year over year in the first quarter and around 20% in subsequent quarters. They also anticipate sequential revenue and profitability growth throughout fiscal 2027.

Demand for nearline HDDs, which are used in data centers and cloud storage, is expected to remain above Seagate's long-term target of mid-20% annual growth in exabyte shipments, the bank said.

The transition from conventional perpendicular magnetic recording (PMR) drives to heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) technology should also support margins through lower costs per terabyte. However, the ramp-up of production yields for Seagate's Mosaic 4+ platform could constrain growth.

Bank of America raised its fiscal 2027 revenue estimate to $18.7 billion from $17.5 billion and its earnings-per-share forecast to $36.53 from $32.06.

Its new $1,200 price target is based on 16 times estimated fiscal 2028 earnings per share of $76.24, reflecting a stronger growth outlook and expectations of margins approaching peak levels. The bank expects favourable pricing and margins to persist into 2028.

However, the firm highlighted five stocks that stand out despite the difficult backdrop.

In a note to clients, BofA analysts warned that calendar third-quarter 2026 earnings present a "tough risk-reward setup" for most companies in their coverage universe. The analysts pointed to multiple headwinds affecting both upstream and downstream chemical producers, including compressed margins, weak demand, and unfavorable currency movements.

For upstream chemical companies, demand has proven quite weak, compressing margins over the monomer level. Some producers have faced difficulty passing through rising raw material and energy costs to customers. Downstream companies are experiencing the tightest window in price-cost spreads as inflation from late first quarter and second quarter finally impacts income statements.

Additional pressures include weaker automotive builds, higher interest rates, and soft residential investment. These factors are eliminating any conservatism companies may have built into their outlooks. A stronger U.S. dollar moving into the fourth quarter adds further headwinds to the sector.

Despite the cautious overall outlook, BofA analysts expressed positive views on five stocks heading into results:

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) has a wealth franchise that deserves attention beyond lending spreads. Second-quarter 2026 Global Wealth and Investment Management net income reached $1.41 billion, roughly 16% of group earnings. That contribution matters when comparing bank stocks favored by billionaires: advisory fees diversify revenue, although rising markets still influence their value.

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) carries an approximately 11x forward P/E against 13x trailing P/E in the September valuation snapshot. Trailing P/E reflects past earnings; forward P/E uses forecasts. Stronger fees, loan growth, and repricing of fixed-rate assets support the earnings outlook. The earnings case rests on converting those revenue gains into profit after compensation, funding costs, and credit losses.

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) looks fairly valued at that multiple, below the approximately 14x forward P/E of JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM), the closest diversified banking comparison. Analysts expect 2027 adjusted EPS growth of approximately 14% versus 4%, respectively. These forecasts exclude specified items and are separate from reported earnings.

Profitability helps explain the peer premium. Second-quarter return on tangible common equity, a non-GAAP measure of profit relative to common equity excluding goodwill and certain intangible assets, was 17% versus 23% at the peer after excluding significant investment gains. Both combine lending, trading, and wealth management, supported by large deposit franchises. Faster expected growth does not erase the difference in returns or exposure to funding costs and credit losses.

title: Family offices eye shift to alternative investments: Study
detail:
Family offices eye shift to alternative investments: Study
The study examined how succession planning is affecting investment · Private Banker International
Vidhya Edwards Munnangi
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:56 AM MST 2 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Nearly four-fifths (79%) of family offices with a prospective next-generation principal anticipate that alternative investments will represent an expanding proportion of their portfolios in the years ahead, according to research from Bank of America.

The study, Building for Generations, examined how succession planning is affecting investment, governance, philanthropy, credit, and technology decisions.

Escalent conducted the research for the 2026 Bank of America Family Office Study, surveying 355 family office decision makers in the US.

It found that 77% of family offices expect philanthropic priorities to change as the next generation takes a greater role.

Private equity remains the largest component of alternative portfolios, representing 27% of allocations.

Notably, 59% of family offices intend to increase private equity exposure over the next three years.

Direct investments are also a focus for long-term wealth creation, with 38% of respondents identified ownership stakes as a leading opportunity, compared with 51% for private equity.

Sports investments are becoming more common.

Four in 10 family offices currently invest in sports, while offices with at least one Gen Z or Millennial principal are the most likely to hold sports teams or sports-related assets.

Governance and family education were widely viewed as important for keeping families aligned on priorities, with 91% agreeing. However, only 40% of offices have a formal family education programme.

Credit is used by 92% of family offices, but only 27% use leverage consistently within a long-term wealth strategy.

The most common uses are supporting real estate investments, cited by 45%; remaining invested through market cycles, at 42%; and meeting short-term liquidity needs, at 38%. Artificial intelligence (AI) is also being adopted across family offices with 42% reported regular employee use of AI, mainly for data analysis, meeting summaries, and automation.

"Family offices eye shift to alternative investments: Study" was originally created and published by Private Banker International, a GlobalData owned brand.

Reflecting On Diversified Banks Stocks' Q3 Earnings: Bank of America (NYSE:BAC)

Quarterly earnings results are a good time to check in on a company's progress, especially compared to its peers in the same sector. Today we are looking at Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) and the best and worst performers in the diversified banks industry.

At their core, diversified banks take in deposits and engage in various forms of lending, which means revenue is generated through interest rate spreads (difference between loan and deposit rates) and fees. Other revenue comes from adjacent services such as wealth management, card and account fees, and products such as annuities. These institutions benefit from rising interest rates that improve NIMs (net interest margins), digital transformation reducing operational costs, and expanding wealth management services as populations age. However, they face headwinds including fintech competition disrupting traditional models (how disruptive is crypto?), stringent regulatory requirements increasing compliance costs, and cybersecurity threats requiring substantial technology investments. Economic downturns also pose risks through potential loan defaults and compressed margins during accommodative monetary policy periods.

The 7 diversified banks stocks we track reported a slower Q3. As a group, revenues missed analysts' consensus estimates by 0.7%.

While some diversified banks stocks have fared somewhat better than others, they have collectively declined. On average, share prices are down 1.8% since the latest earnings results.

Bank of America (NYSE:BAC)

Tracing its roots back to 1784 and now serving approximately 67 million consumer and small business clients, Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) is a global financial institution that provides banking, investing, asset management, and risk management products and services to individuals, businesses, and governments.

Bank of America reported revenues of $30.1 billion, up 3.1% year on year. This print fell short of analysts' expectations by 1.5%. Overall, it was a softer quarter for the company with a significant miss of analysts' EPS estimates and a slight miss of analysts' tangible book value per share estimates.

The market seems disappointed with the results as the stock is down 6.6% since reporting and currently trades at $50.41.

The company sold $2.5 billion of such notes in July 2025 at a 6.25% yield.

Bank of America brought an unusual Friday high-grade bond offering on Oct. 16, braving the market after a turbulent week in credit markets disrupted fundraising plans for numerous borrowers.

Markets are uncertain Tuesday, with a fresh round of AI-fueled worries sending stocks lower and Treasuries higher. A measure of credit risk for US investment-grade bonds rose after logging its highest close since March 31 on Monday.

The firm's shares finished yesterday at their lowest since May 15, extending a post-earnings decline as Bank of America reported that both its stock and fixed-income traders' results fell short of estimates. It also disclosed a $1.2 billion charge for fines for money laundering and sanctions violations.

Bank of America has sold $25 billion of investment-grade notes this year.
